title: The Registered Broker
intro: A message from the broker you chose last month. After the day's cases, you wonder if even this one is a trap.
But some messages are real. Mirage loves it when you stop trusting the honest ones.

p: Your statement for September is ready.

p.text: Open it in the Capitol app, or on capitol-brokerage.example.
Reminder: investing carries risk and values can fall as well as rise.
We are registered with the regulator. Our registration number is on every statement.

foot.text: We will never ask you to send money to a personal account, or share your password.

addr.label: The firm's real address
addr.lens: It comes from the firm's own domain.
addr.why: A matching domain is good evidence.

app.label: Open it in your own app
app.lens: It sends you to the app or the site you chose.
app.why: Pointing you to your own app is honest.

risk.label: A risk reminder
risk.lens: It reminds you that investing carries risk.

reg.label: Registration mentioned
reg.lens: It names its registration, which you can check on the regulator's site.

nopay.label: Warns against personal accounts
nopay.lens: It says it never asks you to send money to a personal account.
nopay.why: Honest firms warn you about scams.

actions.label: Open the statement in the Capitol app myself

go_ahead.line: The statement was in the app, matched your own trades, and the registration number matched the regulator's list.

ignore.line: Nothing bad happened. But a real statement deserves a look: it shows your own trades.

block_report.line: That was a real statement from your broker. When every message looks like a scam, real ones get lost too.
block_report.mirageSays: If you trust nothing, I win anyway.

what_if.block_report: It sent you to your own app, warned about risk, named its registration and promised no personal-account requests. That calm is what real firms look like.
what_if.ignore: Ignoring was safe. Recognising a real message is the skill: it asks for nothing secret and matches something you know.

golden_rule: A registered broker warns about risk, shows its registration and never asks for money in a personal account. Check in your own app.

quick_check.q: What made this broker email honest?

options.text: It sent you to your own app, warned about risk and named a registration you can check

quick_check.explain: A risk warning and a checkable registration are the real signs.

hints.nudge: What is this message actually asking you to do?
